title: Rigveda 1.93: To Agni and Soma
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 1.93: To Agni and Soma: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 1.93 is a hymn of 12 verses addressed to Agni and Soma. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 1, a collection of hymns by many families of poets. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 64v-65v. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 1.93.1-3 (aṣṭaka 1, adhyāya 6, varga 28); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 64v
translation.original_text:
1agnī̍ṣomāv i̱maṁ su me̍ śṛṇu̱taṁ vṛ̍ṣaṇā̱ hava̍m | prati̍ sū̱ktāni̍ haryata̱m bhava̍taṁ dā̱śuṣe̱ maya̍ḥ ||
2agnī̍ṣomā̱ yo a̱dya vā̍m i̱daṁ vaca̍ḥ sapa̱ryati̍ | tasmai̍ dhattaṁ su̱vīrya̱ṁ gavā̱m poṣa̱ṁ svaśvya̍m ||
3agnī̍ṣomā̱ ya āhu̍ti̱ṁ yo vā̱ṁ dāśā̍d dha̱viṣkṛ̍tim | sa pra̱jayā̍ su̱vīrya̱ṁ viśva̱m āyu̱r vy a̍śnavat ||
translation.text:
1AGNI and Soma, mighty Pair, graciously hearken to my call, Accept in friendly wise my hymn, and prosper him who offers gifts.
2The man who honours you to-day, Agni and Soma, with this hymn, Bestow on him heroic strength, increase of kine, and noble steeds.
3The man who offers holy oil and burnt oblations unto you, Agni and Soma, shall enjoy great strength, with offspring, all his life.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 64v (OPenn image 66, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 1.92.15 ‹-aruṇān uṣaḥ atha naḥ›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 65r, begins in RV 1.93.4 ‹bṛsayasya śeṣaḥ avindatam jyotiḥ›. Verses 1.93.1-3 end on this page.

1agnīṣomau | imam | su | me | śṛṇutam | vṛṣaṇā | havam | prati | su-uktāni | haryatam | bhavatam | dāśuṣe | mayaḥ
2agnīṣomā | yaḥ | adya | vām | idam | vacaḥ | saparyati | tasmai | dhattam | su-vīryam | gavām | poṣam | su-aśvyam
3agnīṣomā | yaḥ | āhutim | yaḥ | vām | dāsāt | haviḥ-kṛtim | saḥ | pra-jayā | su-vīryam | viśvam | āyuḥ | vi | aśnavat

translation.original_ref: RV 1.93.4-11 (aṣṭaka 1, adhyāya 6, varga 28); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 65r
translation.original_text:
4agnī̍ṣomā̱ ceti̱ tad vī̱rya̍ṁ vā̱ṁ yad amu̍ṣṇītam ava̱sam pa̱ṇiṁ gāḥ | avā̍tirata̱m bṛsa̍yasya̱ śeṣo 'vi̍ndata̱ṁ jyoti̱r eka̍m ba̱hubhya̍ḥ ||
5yu̱vam e̱tāni̍ di̱vi ro̍ca̱nāny a̱gniś ca̍ soma̱ sakra̍tū adhattam | yu̱vaṁ sindhū̍m̐r a̱bhiśa̍ster ava̱dyād agnī̍ṣomā̱v amu̍ñcataṁ gṛbhī̱tān ||
6ānyaṁ di̱vo mā̍ta̱riśvā̍ jabhā̱rāma̍thnād a̱nyam pari̍ śye̱no adre̍ḥ | agnī̍ṣomā̱ brahma̍ṇā vāvṛdhā̱noruṁ ya̱jñāya̍ cakrathur u lo̱kam ||
7agnī̍ṣomā ha̱viṣa̱ḥ prasthi̍tasya vī̱taṁ harya̍taṁ vṛṣaṇā ju̱ṣethā̍m | su̱śarmā̍ṇā̱ svava̍sā̱ hi bhū̱tam athā̍ dhatta̱ṁ yaja̍mānāya̱ śaṁ yoḥ ||
8yo a̱gnīṣomā̍ ha̱viṣā̍ sapa̱ryād de̍va̱drīcā̱ mana̍sā̱ yo ghṛ̱tena̍ | tasya̍ vra̱taṁ ra̍kṣatam pā̱tam aṁha̍so vi̱śe janā̍ya̱ mahi̱ śarma̍ yacchatam ||
9agnī̍ṣomā̱ save̍dasā̱ sahū̍tī vanata̱ṁ gira̍ḥ | saṁ de̍va̱trā ba̍bhūvathuḥ ||
10agnī̍ṣomāv a̱nena̍ vā̱ṁ yo vā̍ṁ ghṛ̱tena̱ dāśa̍ti | tasmai̍ dīdayatam bṛ̱hat ||
11agnī̍ṣomāv i̱māni̍ no yu̱vaṁ ha̱vyā ju̍joṣatam | ā yā̍ta̱m upa̍ na̱ḥ sacā̍ ||
translation.text:
4Agni and Soma, famed is that your prowess wherewith ye stole the kine, his food, from Paṇi. Ye caused the brood of Br̥isaya to perish; ye found the light, the single light for many.
5Agni and Soma, joined in operation ye have set up the shining lights in heaven. From curse and from reproach, Agni and Soma, ye freed the rivers that were bound in fetters.
6One of you Mitarisvan brought from heaven, the Falcon rent the other from the mountain. Strengthened by holy prayer Agni and Soma have made us ample room for sacrificing.
7Taste, Agni, Soma, this prepared oblation; accept it, Mighty Ones, and let it please you. Vouchsafe us good protection and kind favour: grant to the sacrificer health and riches.
8Whoso with oil and poured oblation honours, with God-devoted heart, Agni and Soma,– Protect his sacrifice, preserve him from distress, grant to the sacrificer great felicity.
9Invoked together, mates in wealth, AgniSoma, accept our hymns: Together be among the Gods.
10Agni and Soma, unto him who worships you with holy oil Shine forth an ample recompense.
11Agni and Soma, be ye pleased with these oblations brought to you, And come, together, nigh to us.

translation.original_ref: RV 1.93.12 (aṣṭaka 1, adhyāya 6, varga 29); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 65v
translation.original_text: <sup>12</sup>agnī̍ṣomā pipṛ̱tam arva̍to na̱ ā pyā̍yantām u̱sriyā̍ havya̱sūda̍ḥ | a̱sme balā̍ni ma̱ghava̍tsu dhattaṁ kṛṇu̱taṁ no̍ adhva̱raṁ śru̍ṣṭi̱manta̍m ||
translation.text: <sup>12</sup>Agni and Soma, cherish well our horses, and let our cows be fat who yield oblations. Grant power to us and to our wealthy patrons, and cause our holy rites to be successful.
